transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m here mostly because that clinic for the logistics job, you know, the clearance thing, said my weight was too low to pass me through. Which seemed kind of ridiculous to me, honestly. I mean, in that line of work you don’t want to be dragging around extra pounds—gotta stay quick on your feet, move boxes, pallets, all that. I’ve done labor work long enough to know lean is useful. So… they told me I had to come get checked out, but I don’t really see the issue the way they do.
Can you tell me about your eating habits lately? Have you been eating enough or have you been intentionally losing weight?

I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m trying to lose weight exactly. I just… I keep things pretty light. Most days it’s black coffee, maybe a boiled egg, sometimes a little tuna if I’ve got it around. And if I’m not actually moving freight that day, I figure I don’t really need a full meal, you know?

People act like you have to eat three big meals just because the clock says so, but that never made sense to me. Back when I was loading trailers, you learned real quick what slows you down. So I just eat what I think I need.
Do you ever feel like you're not eating enough, or do you feel a strong lack of appetite even when you're not working?

I don’t know if I’d call it not eating enough. I just don’t get the point of forcing it, especially on days I’m not actually moving freight. Most days I’ll do black coffee, maybe a boiled egg, or a little tuna if I’ve got some. That seems like enough if I’m not burning it off.

Back when I was on busier shifts, guys would eat these huge lunches and then complain they felt heavy all afternoon. I always thought, well, that’s your problem right there. So I guess… appetite-wise, I can ignore it pretty easy. I just tell myself I don’t need a real meal unless there’s real work to do.
Do you ever feel anxious or upset about eating more than you plan, or do you avoid eating in front of others because of your habits?

Yeah, I mean… I don’t like eating more than I meant to, if that’s what you mean. Especially stuff like rice or bread, or anything greasy. It’s funny, back when I was working docks, guys would bring these big sandwiches dripping with oil, and then everyone wonders why they’re sluggish by two o’clock.

But yeah, if I eat something like that, it kind of stays in my head. I’ll think, well, that’s just going to sit on me now. Then the next morning I might check the scale, or see how my belt feels, just to make sure I didn’t… you know, let myself go. I don’t make a big scene about it, but it bothers me.
